title: How to Build a Welcome Flow That Actually Converts
excerpt: Most welcome flows are a discount email and silence. Build the five-email version: promise, story, proof, objection, and deadline, with plain-language metrics.
body: The welcome flow is the highest-traffic email sequence a store ever runs, because every new subscriber passes through it, and most stores waste it with a single discount email followed by silence. New subscribers are at peak interest: they just raised their hand. A five-email flow captures that interest without feeling like pressure, and building it takes an afternoon in any mainstream email platform.

Email one goes out immediately and has one job: deliver the promised incentive and set expectations. State plainly what they get, when the next email arrives, and what kind of content to expect. The discount code goes here with an expiry window long enough to browse, typically seven days. This email routinely produces the highest open rate your list will ever see, often above fifty percent, which is exactly why it should carry clear expectations rather than just a coupon blast.

Email two arrives on day two and tells the brand story through the customer's problem, not your founding myth. Lead with the specific problem your product solves, show how you approached it differently, and link one product collection that matches the segment the subscriber came from, since someone who signed up from a skincare page does not need a link to your full catalog. Personalizing this link by signup source is the highest-leverage automation detail in the whole flow.

Email three, day four, is proof. Stack three short customer reviews against the product collection from email two, and include one review that mentions an objection, because honest criticism quoted verbatim converts better than perfect praise. Email four, day six, is the objection handler: answer the three most common pre-purchase questions from your support inbox, shipping, sizing, guarantee, in plain sentences. If your support queue does not know its top three questions, ask it; the answers are already written in your replies.

Email five, day eight or nine, closes the incentive window honestly. A deadline reminder with the expiring code, a restatement of the bestseller with social proof, and a clean unsubscribe-friendly sign-off. Urgency only works when it is real, and a code that actually expires builds more trust than one that quietly renews forever.

Measure three numbers: flow completion rate, revenue per recipient, and unsubscribe rate. A healthy flow converts at several times your batch campaigns and unsubscribes well under one percent per email. Platforms like Omnisend ship welcome flow templates with this structure built in, and the tool page at /tool/omnisend details its automation pricing tiers. The DTCwise Email and SMS category at /category/email-sms compares platforms on flow features so you can pick the builder that fits your stack, then let the sequence run and compound quietly in the background.
